verses.1: Not to us, LORD, not to us but to your name give glory because of your faithfulness and love.
verses.2: Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?"
verses.3: Our God is in heaven; whatever God wills is done.
verses.4: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
verses.5: They have mouths but do not speak, eyes but do not see.
verses.6: They have ears but do not hear, noses but do not smell.
verses.7: They have hands but do not feel, feet but do not walk, and no sound rises from their throats.
verses.8: Their makers shall be like them, all who trust in them.
verses.9: The house of Israel trusts in the LORD, who is their help and shield.
verses.10: The house of Aaron trusts in the LORD, who is their help and shield.
verses.11: Those who fear the LORD trust in the LORD, who is their help and shield.
verses.12: The LORD remembers us and will bless us, will bless the house of Israel, will bless the house of Aaron,
verses.13: Will bless those who fear the LORD, small and great alike.
verses.14: May the LORD increase your number, you and your descendants.
verses.15: May you be blessed by the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
verses.16: The heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth is given to us.
verses.17: The dead do not praise the LORD, all those gone down into silence.
verses.18: It is we who bless the LORD, both now and forever. Hallelujah!

notes.text: Where is their God?: implies that God cannot help them.

The house of Israel... the house of Aaron... those fear the LORD: the laity of Israelite birth, the priests, and the converts to Judaism. Cf Psalm 118:2-4; 135:19-21. In the New Testament likewise "those who fear the Lord" means converts to Judaism (cf Acts 10:2, 22, 35; 13:16, 26).
The heavens: literally "the heaven of heavens" or "the highest heavens," i.e., above the firmament. See note on Psalm 148:4.
